resources.string:
Changes apply at once but are lost on reset until you tap Save to robot.

1. Balance angle: hold the robot upright at the point where it balances by itself, with Motors off, and tap Use mean angle. Wrong value = it keeps creeping one way.

2. Angle loop: set Speed Kp and Speed Ki to 0. Raise Angle Kp until the robot stands but buzzes or shakes quickly, then back off about 40%. Raise Angle Kd until the shaking stops; too much Kd shows up as jitter (spiky Gyro and PWM).

3. Speed loop: put the kit's Speed Kp back and set Speed Ki to Speed Kp / 50. If it drifts away, raise Speed Kp; if it rocks slowly back and forth, lower it.

4. Watch PWM saturation in the stats: above a few % means the motors are at their limit and the robot is close to falling.

Record CSV saves the telemetry to Android/data/com.zyc0049.balancetuner/files on the phone.

The robot tries gains on its own while it balances on the floor (~1 m free, USB cable slack); stand it up again whenever it falls. Each trial is scored by a cost (wobble, gyro, wheel drift and travel, PWM saturation; a fall is worst).

ML (Bayesian): a Gaussian-process model learns the cost from every trial and picks the most promising next one; about 15–25 trials for two gains.
Twiddle: the PC autotune.py search: one gain at a time, ±25 % steps that grow after a win and shrink otherwise; a win is measured twice before it is kept. Stays close to the current gains.

Tick Balance angle to search it too (within ±3°; steps in degrees for Twiddle). Range × sets the gains' search box (current ÷ range … × range); picking a method sets its default. Each trial nudges the robot forward and back (Nudge 0 = none). Trials go to ml_tune_log.csv next to the CSV recordings.
